description: pkix-lint/src/cabf_tls_br.rs:255: check 'n_bytes >= 256' passes a 2047-bit modulus (256 bytes, no leading 0x00 since high bit is 0) as compliant with the 2048-bit minimum. The doc comment acknowledges this but claims it matches zlint behavior. CA/B Forum TLS BR §6.1.5 requires >= 2048 bits strictly; 2047-bit keys should fail. The same bug exists in pkix-path/src/lib.rs:rsa_public_key_bits where UintRef::as_bytes() strips the leading sign byte so the bit count is magnitude_bytes*8, flooring a 2048-bit key (2048 bits, 256 magnitude bytes) to 2048. Actually wait — rsa_public_key_bits returns magnitude bytes * 8, and a 2048-bit key has 256 magnitude bytes (UintRef strips 0x00) → 2048 bits — this path is correct. But the lint uses raw DER length (including 0x00), so a 2047-bit key (256 DER bytes) passes. The two paths disagree: pkix-path rejects 2047-bit keys (magnitude = 256 bytes → 2048 reported, passes min_rsa_key_bits=2048), while the lint passes 2047-bit keys.
title: RsaMinKeySizeLint accepts 2047-bit RSA keys as passing the 2048-bit floor
